results.pageText: "The quickest, most direct way to get money in people's pockets is for the government to take less out in the first place," Hilton said.

I support affordable housing that keeps families, seniors, artists and workers in District 4, including intergenerational artistic housing and cooperative business initiatives that strengthen neighborhoods and help residents age with dignity.

At the same time, Muni has to use existing dollars well and be accountable for service, reliability, and the rider experience, because San Franciscans deserve a system that is both sustainable and dependable.

Dion-Jay "DJ" Brookter Job: Former chief executive officer at Young Community Developers Age: 43 Residency: Homeowner since 2021, lived in Candlestick Point since 2014 Transportation: Driving, public transit, walking Education: Bachelor's degree from Utah State University, MBA from University of Phoenix Languages: English, some Spanish My top priority is addressing San Francisco's affordability crisis so the people who built our communities can afford to remain, succeed, and thrive here.
We can not tax our way out of MUNI's funding crisis.
I bring experience, accountability and the commitment to make every dollar count for the community.
